references.text: The parallel account in Mark describes the same scene: the people come and find the demon-possessed man sitting, clothed and in his right mind, and they are afraid.
The parallel account in Matthew tells that the whole town went out to meet Jesus after the healing of the demon-possessed men.
The entire account of the demon-possessed man in the region of the Gerasenes in Mark provides the most detailed parallel to Luke's account, including the man's condition before and after the healing.
Earlier in the same account, the man's condition before the healing is described—naked and without a home—which stands in sharp contrast to his now sitting clothed and in his right mind.
In the account of the woman who was healed from bleeding, she also falls at Jesus' feet, just as the healed man here sits at Jesus' feet in gratitude and submission.
After the healing, the man wants to follow Jesus, but Jesus sends him home to testify—this shows the transformation that people witnessed in verse 15.
Isaiah speaks of God coming to save, and those who are afraid will be strengthened—Jesus' power over demons demonstrates God's saving power, which awakens both reverence and fear in the onlookers.
Also when Jesus raised the widow's son in Nain, the people were seized with fear and praised God. The reaction of fear is a recurring theme when people are confronted with God's power through Jesus.
Peter falls at Jesus' feet after the miraculous catch of fish and asks Jesus to go away, seized by fear—a parallel reaction to the fear that grips the people here.
